subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename workspace files as a supported `bootstrap-extra-files` hook contract?
rationale: This expands deterministic system-prompt context and file-loading scope, which is a product and security-boundary choice rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Approve guarded custom files
options.body: Allow custom basenames only when explicitly configured and still protected by workspace containment, size budgets, ordering, diagnostics, and session filtering.

options.title: Keep recognized basenames only
options.body: Reject arbitrary bootstrap-file injection and steer users toward first-class filename proposals or workspace convention docs instead.

options.title: Defer to broader context design
options.body: Leave this issue open until maintainers settle a larger context-files or capability-discovery API.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded custom files
recommendation.body: Allow custom basenames only when explicitly configured and still protected by workspace containment, size budgets, ordering, diagnostics, and session filtering.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the original hook feature and is the best available routing owner for the product boundary decision.
